traceability.notes:
All specified acceptance criteria for story 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are implemented and verified: - Core functionality is present via nested `story`/`req` and flat `storyPathPattern` / `requirementIdPattern` options in the valid-annotation-format rule, with configuration helpers and schema support. - Backward compatibility is preserved through default regex patterns and examples that are used when no options are provided or when options are invalid. - Pattern validation is performed by attempting to construct RegExp instances and collecting configuration errors, which are reported through the `invalidRuleConfiguration` message without stopping annotation validation. - Error messages incorporate optional example strings (`story.example`/`req.example` and flat shorthand), proven by tests that assert the exact message text when custom examples are configured. - Configuration quality is enforced with a clear JSON Schema (via getRuleSchema) that defines both nested and flat fields and disallows unknown properties, matching ESLint best practices. - The behavior is compatible with the existing valid-story-reference rule: valid-annotation-format focuses on syntactic patterns for story and requirement identifiers, while valid-story-reference handles file existence and storyDirectories; both are configurable so users can align them for their project layout. - Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md clearly explains nested and flat configuration fields, defaults, invalid configuration handling, and provides concrete examples, covering the documentation acceptance criterion.
All relevant unit tests tied to this story pass in the project’s Jest run, so the implementation for this story is considered complete and correct.
